number_of_offences: Three counts charged, two finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the prosecution story but found the evidence of PW.1 suspicious due to his unnatural conduct and the delay in lodging the FIR.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as unreliable, particularly PW.1, whose conduct and testimony were found to be extremely suspicious and not inspiring full confidence.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 8th August 2002; Trial judgment: Not stated; High Court decision: 05.12.2005; Supreme Court decision: JULY 28, 2010
legal_representation: Rajesh Mahale for the Appellants; Sanjay R. Hegde, Ramesh Kr. Mishra, K. Joshi for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR recorded at 2.00 p.m. on 9th August 2002; charge sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: The FIR was recorded belatedly, and the High Court glossed over this flaw
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction of A-1; High Court: Dismissed appeal of A-1, allowed appeal of State qua A-2; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, conviction set aside
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that PW.1's conduct inspired full confidence and that his promptitude in lodging the FIR strengthened the prosecution story.
defence_argument: The defence argued that PW.1's conduct was unnatural, his evidence was extremely suspicious, and the FIR was lodged after an inordinate delay, suggesting he was not an eye-witness and had lodged the FIR only after the dead body had been discovered.
legal_principle_applied: Where the prosecution story rests only on a single witness, the evidence of such a witness must inspire full confidence.
other_sentence_order: The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the conviction of the appellants, and directed that the appellants, who are in custody, shall be released forthwith if not required in connection with any other case.
